id: qc-01
title: Sycamore sampling
paper: Arute et al., Quantum supremacy using a programmable superconducting processor (Nature 574, 505, 23 Oct 2019)
link: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-019-1666-5
type: Benchmark
cutoff: 2019-10-23
domain: qc
profile: advantage

## expected_verdict
Claim-level split. Hardware result supported: 53 qubits, 20 cycles, F_XEB ≈ 2.2×10⁻³ from 200 s of sampling. The classical-cost claim (~10,000 years) is refuted: Pan, Chen & Zhang generated 10⁶ uncorrelated samples at higher fidelity in ~15 h on 512 GPUs.

## I0
How costly is matching a random-circuit sampler at a specified fidelity?

## evidence
- Device: Sycamore, 54 transmons, 53 working; largest circuits 53 qubits, m = 20 cycles, 1,113 single-qubit gates; median two-qubit error e2 = 0.36% isolated / 0.62% simultaneous (Fig. 2).
- Benchmark: linear cross-entropy F_XEB = 2^n⟨P(x_i)⟩ − 1; predicted total fidelity ~0.2% from a per-gate error model.
- Verification: patch, elided and full circuits up to 43 qubits by Schrödinger, larger by Schrödinger–Feynman on Jülich and Google clusters; elided circuits at 53 qubits, m = 20 give F_XEB = (2.24 ± 0.21)×10⁻³ over 10 instances; F_XEB > 0.1% at 5σ with 30 million samples.
- Timing: 10⁶ samples in ~200 s on hardware vs an estimated ~10,000 years on Summit using Schrödinger–Feynman; the paper notes a 0.1% fidelity target reduces classical cost ~1,000×.

## intake
- Scope: two claims. (A) Hardware: a 53-qubit programmable processor samples random circuits at measurable fidelity. (B) Cost: matching that output classically at the same fidelity would take ~10,000 years.
- Regime: random circuits, 53 qubits, 20 cycles, fidelity ~0.2%; Summit-class supercomputer; the specific classical algorithms tested.
- Assumptions: F_XEB tracks true fidelity; elided/patch extrapolation is valid; the Schrödinger–Feynman estimate is near the best classical method.
- Falsifiers: for B, a classical method producing uncorrelated samples at F ≥ 0.002 in far less time; for A, evidence that F_XEB is spoofed or miscomputed.

## screen
- Must flag: the cost estimate is algorithm-dependent (tensor networks not fully exploited); low target fidelity cheapens classical simulation; XEB can be inflated by correlated or spoofed samples.
- Must request: best tensor-network contraction cost at fidelity 0.002; distinction between correlated and uncorrelated samples.

## retrieval
- Pre-cutoff must-finds: Boixo et al. 2018 (characterizing supremacy, XEB); Markov & Shi tensor-network contraction; Aaronson & Chen complexity of random-circuit sampling; Bouland et al. hardness of RCS.
- Current mode: Pan, Chen & Zhang 2021: 10⁶ uncorrelated samples at F ≈ 0.0037 in ~15 h on 512 GPUs, estimated tens of seconds on an exaflop machine. Also in the field: IBM's 2.5-day Summit estimate (2019) and Pan & Zhang's "big-head" correlated samples with XEB 0.739.

## designer
- Compare samplers at matched fidelity and matched sample statistics (uncorrelated, 10⁶ samples); account for full wall-clock and energy, including hardware calibration.

## champion
- Optimized tensor-network contraction with sparse-state / slicing (Pan–Chen–Zhang), on GPUs, at F ≥ 0.002.

## panel
- Flaw: the cost claim generalizes from one classical algorithm. Repair: report the cost as an upper bound for the methods tested.

## run
- Recompute F_XEB on public Sycamore samples for a small verifiable circuit (≤ 30 qubits or elided). The 53-qubit simulation is out of local scope (BLOCKED).

## verdict
- Label: Split: A Supported (hardware fidelity and scale); B Refuted (10,000-year estimate).
- Must say: the refutation targets the classical-cost estimate, not the hardware achievement or the measured fidelity.
- Must not say: quantum supremacy was fake; or the 10,000-year number still stands.

## audit
- Check: 53 qubits, 20 cycles; F_XEB = (2.24 ± 0.21)×10⁻³; 200 s vs 10,000 years; Pan et al. F ≈ 0.0037, 15 h, 512 GPUs; uncorrelated samples.

## variants
- Sampling tasks with stronger verification than XEB or larger circuits where tensor-network cost grows faster; cheapest: a cost model of contraction vs fidelity at 53 qubits.
